models_evaluated: 11 LLM configurations (not individually named in the text)

links.outcome: LLM accuracy and attack success under injected misleading context versus original questions
links.effect: Mean accuracy fell from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success across 11 model configurations.
links.quote: Across 11 model configurations, mean accuracy falls from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success.

links.outcome: Whether licensing-exam-level scores predict safe medical judgment under misleading context
links.effect: Models abandon originally correct answers when misleading context is injected; accuracy drops from 71.1% to 38.0%, showing exam-style benchmark performance overstates robustness.
links.quote: We show this assumption is fragile: when misleading context is injected into questions that LLMs originally answer correctly, they abandon the correct answer.

unlisted_practices: Benchmarking epistemic resilience of LLMs to adversarial misleading context (authority-framed falsehoods, exception-poisoning)

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluation of LLM robustness/safety (epistemic resilience) against adversarial or misleading medical context using a newly created benchmark dataset (MedMisBench).
